title: Finite algebras over Hausdorff extremally disconnected affine spectra
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and R -> S an algebra map. Assume S is finite as an R-module and finitely presented as an R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose Spec R [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is Hausdorff and extremally disconnected, and every residue field kappa(p), for p in Spec R, is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]. Then Spec S is extremally disconnected. No flatness, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0985, Lemma 61.11.5, finite case; expand the decomposition using the finite affine section-cover theorem (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0985).

proof.text: Apply exists_finite_affine_section_cover to f:Spec S → Spec R. Install the resulting affine, finite locally free and closed immersion structures. Finite affine morphisms with Hausdorff target have Hausdorff source: transport to spectra of global sections, contract each prime to a maximal prime, apply integral going up, and use Spec.profinite_of_isMaximal. All affine spaces are compact.

For affine f and g, finite presentation of f ≫ g and finite type of g imply finite presentation of f by RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_comp_finiteType on global sections. Apply this to j ≫ p and i_k ≫ p. Chevalley makes their images constructible. Induction on constructible sets shows that they are clopen in compact Hausdorff spaces: a retrocompact open is compact and hence closed; union and complement preserve clopenness. Thus j and i_k are open embeddings on points. The clopen preimages V_k=j^(-1)(image i_k) cover Y_prime, and snd restricted to V_k is an open embedding by factoring through the inverse of the section chart i_k. These arguments are proved in the private locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp_affine, isClopen_of_isConstructible, isClopen_range_of_finitePresentation and openEmbedding_on_preimage_section helpers.

Use exists_continuous_section_of_surjective to choose a continuous section sigma of a:X_prime → X. Form the closed topological pullback P={(y_prime,x) | snd(y_prime)=sigma(x)}. Its open clopen charts over V_k project bijectively and continuously onto the open subsets sigma^(-1)(snd(V_k)) of X. Compact-to-Hausdorff bijections are homeomorphisms. Open subspaces of extremally disconnected spaces are extremally disconnected, and the property is local on open covers, as proved using closure/preimage identities. Hence P is extremally disconnected, by the private extremallyDisconnected_pullback_of_sections helper.

Prove P → Y bijective. Existence of scheme pullback points gives surjectivity. For injectivity, a point of P over y has x=f(y) by pullback.condition and a(sigma(x))=x. Its two scheme pullback projections are therefore determined by y. The private pullbackPoint_ext lemma identifies two such points using subsingleton tensor spectra over separably closed residue fields. Its residue-integrality hypothesis follows from finite_residueFieldMap_of_finite: every prime of S is maximal, its residue field is module-finite over S and hence over R, and restriction of scalars gives finiteness over the residue field of R; the existing AlgebraicGeometry.finite_spec_residueFieldMap from IntegralClosureDedekindSurjectiveFibres transports this calculation through the affine stalk isomorphisms. Transport separable closedness through Spec.residueFieldIso using isSepClosed_of_ringEquiv.

The continuous bijection P → Y is a homeomorphism because P is compact and Y Hausdorff. Transport the proved extremal disconnectedness of P along this homeomorphism. No disjoint refinement, section equalizer locus or sigma-type decomposition is needed; empty spaces and empty charts are handled by the same constructions.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0985, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-over-extremally-disconnected, finite case. Group A2 formalized the finite affine section-cover route, replacing Boolean partitioning with clopen section charts and locality of extremal disconnectedness. Repair: reuse the existing affine residue-field finiteness transport theorem, exported in its original module, instead of duplicating it.
